intro: At base camp the stove throws a thin orange light onto the biscuit tin, and the tin still smells of tallow, salt and the wet wool of the sleeping bags piled above it. The ship went down in the pack ice in the first winter; what we have are the messages one by one in that tin, each in a different hand and each written as if the writer trusted no reader. Old Joss keeps the watch-keeper's ledger by the stove, and its only habit is to give every line two figures and nothing else: the day, then the bell. We have read the messages aloud by turns, and the new ones arrive folded inside the tin lid, smudged with grease and smelling of the seals. No one has opened the tin in daylight for weeks.
echo: Dig down a foot and the ground has been frozen since the mammoths.

puzzles.title: Frost Smoke

blocks.text: The knight sets out from g5: Nh7 Nf6 Ng4 Nh2 Nf3 Nd4 Nb5 Nc7 Na8 Nb6.

hints: Those are chess moves. Which squares does the piece land on, and what's written there?
Start on the given square, play each move, and read the letter on every square it lands on.

puzzles.title: Pack Ice
puzzles.flavor: Nothing was lost; everything simply moved over.
hints: Every letter is close to the right one. Close on what? Look down at your hands.
QWERTY: every letter was typed one key to the side. Try shifting each one back, both directions.

puzzles.title: Sastrugi
hints: A familiar grid puzzle in unfamiliar clothes. Once it's done, are some squares more important than others?
Solve it like a sudoku, then read the numbered squares in order.

puzzles.title: Winter Quarters
puzzles.flavor: The radio operator had everything back to front, but only from A to Z.
hints: Each word stands for a letter, the way radio operators spell. Do those letters read? If not, try the alphabet backwards.
Take the NATO call signs' initials, then swap each letter for its mirror: A for Z, B for Y.

puzzles.title: Dead Reckoning
puzzles.flavor: Through the wall: bursts of knocks, always in pairs.
hints: Always two numbers, never more than five. How would two prisoners spell through a wall with a 5×5 grid?
Tap code: the first count is the row, the second the column, in a 5×5 alphabet with no K.

puzzles.title: Polar Plateau
puzzles.flavor: Everything came out of the wash with a little something extra.
hints: Each jumble is almost a word from this round, but with a letter to spare. Which letter, every time?
Rearrange each into a theme word; the spare letters, in order, are the answer.

meta.title: Meta: The Last Expedition
hints: Every entry has two numbers. What in this round is numbered, and what could the second number count?
The first number picks a puzzle; the second picks a letter inside its answer.
